name: grip-detect
_comment: Example rule graph for the on-device rule engine (the `rules` app).
Nodes evaluate in array order and may only reference EARLIER nodes by
their index via "in", which is what makes a cycle impossible to write.
Every operator has a fixed per-frame cost, so the engine computes the
whole graph's worst case at load time and refuses anything that would
not fit inside the frame budget -- an over-budget graph is rejected
before it can cost a single sample.

nodes._: 0: total force over the whole mat
1: force in the palm region only (rows 4-9, cols 4-9)
2: how many cells are actually being touched (kPressureActiveThreshold)

3: palm loaded? values are calibrated millivolts (see kPressureFullScale=2000 per cell), NOT 0..1 -- a 36-cell region under firm pressure sums into the thousands. Hysteresis stops it chattering on the threshold.
4: require the grip to be held for 120ms before believing it
5: fire on both edges of the debounced grip
